content: For adults and children weighing more than 20 kg, the standard dosage for genitourinary or gastrointestinal tract infections, excluding gonorrhea, is 500 mg administered four times daily (qid) at evenly spaced intervals. In cases of severe or chronic infections, higher doses may be necessary. For the treatment of gonorrhea in both men and women, a single oral dose of 3.5 grams of ampicillin should be given concurrently with 1 gram of probenecid. It is critical that physicians do not prescribe less than the recommended dosage for gonorrhea treatment. Follow-up cultures should be obtained from the original infection site(s) 7 to 14 days after completing therapy. In women, it is advisable to perform culture tests from both the endocervical and anal canals to confirm eradication. Complications such as prostatitis and epididymitis require prolonged and intensive therapy. For respiratory tract infections, the usual dosage is 250 mg administered four times daily (qid) at evenly spaced intervals. For children weighing 20 kg or less, the standard dosage for genitourinary or gastrointestinal tract infections is 100 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, divided into four equal doses administered at evenly spaced intervals. For respiratory tract infections, the recommended dosage is 50 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, divided into three or four equal doses administered at evenly spaced intervals. Pediatric doses should not exceed the maximum doses recommended for adults. For all patients, regardless of age or weight, higher doses may be required for severe or chronic infections. Except for the single-dose regimen used for gonorrhea, treatment should continue for at least 48 to 72 hours after the patient becomes asymptomatic or after bacterial eradication has been confirmed. For infections caused by hemolytic strains of streptococci, a minimum of 10 days of treatment is necessary to reduce the risk of complications such as rheumatic fever or glomerulonephritis. In cases of chronic urinary or gastrointestinal infections, frequent bacteriological and clinical evaluations are required during therapy and may need to continue for several months after treatment. Persistent infections may necessitate treatment for several weeks. Dosages lower than those specified above should not be used.
